evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/dashboard/hooks/useActionQueue.ts:240-300 — the dashboard Action Queue is entirely mock-backed on a shipped surface, not TODO-gated dead code. The useQuery queryFn returns generateMockData(role) after a setTimeout(300) 'simulate network delay' (the real fetch is commented out at :243-245), and the executeAction useMutation (:283) is a no-op setTimeout(500) that returns { success: true } with the real POST commented out (:284-288). dismissItem (:300) and handleAction (:308) both route through this stub mutation, whose onSuccess invalidates the query so the UI reports success and re-renders more fabricated items.

Reachable in production: consumed by frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/dashboard/components/ActionQueue.tsx:40 (useActionQueue(userRole, filters)) — a rendered dashboard component for both 'manager' and 'resident' roles. Failure scenario: managers/residents see a fabricated action list (fake urgent/high counts) and 'dismiss'/'execute' actions silently do nothing server-side while the UI confirms success — a fully stubbed primary-dashboard feature masquerading as live.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/compliance/pages/ContentModerationPage.tsx:128-146 — handleTakeAction() collects the moderation action via window.prompt('Enter action type (remove, restrict, warn, approve):') and passes the free-text result straight into the mutation as `action_type: actionType as 'remove' | 'restrict' | 'warn' | 'approve'`. The `as` cast crosses the API boundary and lies to the type checker: any string the operator types (typo, 'REMOVE', 'delete') passes compile-time and is sent to takeAction against the compliance backend with no client-side enum validation. handleDecideAppeal (:167+) has the same shape ('uphold'/'overturn' via prompt). AmlDashboardPage.tsx:107/134 repeats the window.prompt pattern for EDD/review actions.

Compounding UX/completeness gap: handleViewContent (:160) uses window.location.href for in-app navigation (full page reload inside an SPA) instead of the router. All flagged in-code as TODO(Phase-2). Failure scenario: an invalid action_type reaches the compliance-moderation mutation (rejected server-side at best, mis-applied at worst) on a legally-sensitive DSA moderation surface, and the free-text-cast defeats the SDK's typed enum contract.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/settings/pages/SessionsPage.tsx:84 — `const sessions = (sessionsQuery.data?.sessions ?? []) as unknown as SessionRow[];` force-casts the auth API sessions response to the local SessionRow[] via the double `as unknown as` escape hatch, bypassing all structural checking between the generated SDK type and SessionRow. Immediately after, code reads `s.isCurrent` (:85, and current-session highlighting / revoke UI downstream). If the SDK field is snake_case (is_current) or the shape drifts, `s.isCurrent` is silently undefined, so 'this device' detection and the revoke-all-other-sessions affordance can mis-identify the current session on a security-sensitive session-management screen. The cast hides exactly the kind of API-contract drift the generated client exists to catch.
